name: M1 -> the amended D100 is reverted to the FIRST cut of E1: the anchor goes back to the athlete's MILE pace instead of their own row read at the goal distance. The mile the athlete entered still reaches the clock, so nothing looks missing — a 1.5-mile goal simply starts at a pace the athlete only holds for a mile, which is the defect coach amended the ruling to remove
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 P1d, the row that says the anchor equals the mile column at or below one mile and is STRICTLY SLOWER past it. P1d is the declared target rather than P1 because it fails on the SHAPE of the amendment and needs no agreement on a single interpolated second, so it cannot be satisfied by a gate whose hand chart drifted. P1 must go red with it (288 of 360 builds have a goal past a mile) and P1c too. EXPECTED COLLATERAL, DISCLOSED: P5b goes red — this is the mutation that brings the 138 flat-parked builds back, which is the measured reason the ruling was amended — and the pinned row goes with it: Q2, Q2b, Q5, Q7, Q8. Q3 stays GREEN (the TARGET wiring is untouched) and R1..R5 stay GREEN, because rowPaceAt is still present and still correct; it has merely stopped being called. A suite that only tested the helper would ship this mutant. P1b goes red on the beginner segment too: the beginner's 690 ROW stops converting. B1 GREEN.

name: M2 -> the beginner guard is dropped from the single place that computes the entered mile in seconds. D100 still fires, the anchor still wins for everyone — including the beginner, who under the V172 rule must keep the 690 s/mi experience default no matter what mile time they typed
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 P1b, which must read red over the 120 beginner builds in the sweep, every one of which anchors on the typed mile instead of 690. WHY THIS MUTATION EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM M1: M1 removes the new behaviour, M2 over-applies it. D100's form is 'the entered anchor wins for non-beginner' and only a mutation in this direction can show that the gate tests the GATE on the rule and not merely the presence of _mileBestSecs in the expression. P1 goes red with it (the beginner rows now miss their hand-expected 690), which is why P1b is the declared target: P1b is the row that names WHICH segment broke. EXPECTED COLLATERAL: the pinned row is intermediate, so Q2..Q8 all stay GREEN — this mutant ships a correct PRT TING program and a wrong beginner program, and a suite that only pinned PRT TING would pass it. B1 stays GREEN (HALF_MANNY is NRC). Note the mutated line also feeds _anchorSec for the pace-chart lookup; that is the same defect seen twice, not a leak.

name: M3 -> D101 is reverted: the age-scaled table value is multiplied by 2.5 again and capped at a 12 s/mi/wk ceiling, so a compressed timeline once more promises an athlete up to 12 seconds per mile per week. Both unsourced numbers come back exactly as V201 carried them
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 P4, the row that says no build improves faster than the age-scaled hand table allows. It must go red on the dampened segment of the sweep and print a first miss whose gain is a multiple of 2.5 above the table (for example intermediate/18-35 gain 12 against a table of 5). P4b must go red with it: 'every dampened build improves at EXACTLY the table rate' is the positive form of the same claim and is what stops P4 being satisfiable by a merely smaller wrong number. P4c must STAY GREEN — the dampened branch still fires; if P4c went red the sweep would have stopped exercising the branch and P4/P4b would be vacuous. EXPECTED COLLATERAL, DISCLOSED: Q4 (pinned gain 5), Q5, Q7 and Q8 go red, because the pinned after-grid is the rate applied; Q2 and Q3 stay GREEN, which separates D101 from D100 in the report. P5 stays GREEN: the array is still internally consistent with whatever rate was chosen, and that is exactly why P5 alone could never have caught this. B1 GREEN.

name: M4 -> E2 is half-reverted: the entered goal stops reaching the progression (arguments[9] and [10] go back to null) while ageBracket keeps flowing. The progression falls back to its own internal guess of initialPace x 0.85, so the athlete is walked toward a target nobody entered, from the correct starting pace
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 P2, which must read 0 of 360 — every build now targets 0.85 x the anchor instead of the seconds and distance the athlete typed — with a first miss of the form 'mi/1.5/10:30 got 420.75 want 420.0000'. P3 must go red with it: P3 is the equality row the ruling demanded (the sizer's tPacePerMile and the progression's _targetPace must be ONE number), and this mutation is precisely the state V201 was in, where the block was sized on the entered goal and paced on a guess. P3b must STAY GREEN: paceGoalTarget still exists and is still callable, so a gate that only checked for the helper's presence would pass this mutant. EXPECTED COLLATERAL: Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8 red (the pinned after-grid is the entered target applied); Q2 GREEN (the anchor still wins), which is the D100 halves separating cleanly. P1, P1b, P1c GREEN. B1 GREEN.

name: M5 -> a SECOND arithmetic for the same conversion, which is the exact defect the ruling forbids. The single reader keeps its shape but converts kilometres through 1/1.609344 instead of the ruled 0.621, so every km athlete is sized and paced on a distance that differs from the ruled one in the fourth significant figure. Nothing about the code reads wrong on sight
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 P2, red on the km half of the sweep (180 of 360 builds) and green on the mi half, with a first miss on a km row. THIS IS THE MUTATION P2's HAND CONVERSION EXISTS FOR: the gate types MI_PER_KM = 0.621 itself, so moving the app's factor moves one side only. If the gate had asked the app for its constant, or compared the progression against the sizer alone, both sides would move together and this mutant would survive — which is why P3 is NOT the declared target here: P3 compares sizer against progression against hand value, and it goes red only because of its hand-value limb. P3 red is therefore EXPECTED COLLATERAL and confirms the hand limb is live. Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q7, Q8 stay GREEN: the pinned PRT TING cfg is a MILE cfg and is untouched, so this is the second mutant in the file that ships a correct pinned row and a wrong program. B1 GREEN. Gatekeeper: confirm the km/mi SPLIT in the miss list, not merely that P2 went red; a P2 that went red on mi rows too would mean the mutation reached the wrong path.

name: M6 -> ageBracket stops reaching the progression: the call site hard-codes 18-35, so a 55-plus athlete is handed the 18-35 rate. The D101 cap is still a single number with no multiplier and no ceiling, and it is still the table value — just always the wrong row of the table for anyone over 35
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 P4, red on the 36-54 and 55+ segments of the sweep (240 of 360 builds are in those two brackets) where the dampened rate now exceeds the age-scaled hand table — an advanced 55+ athlete improving at 7.0 s/mi/wk against a table of 4.55. P4b red with it for the same reason. P4d is the row that says the rate still VARIES with experience and age; gatekeeper should read it, because a collapse of the age dimension is exactly what this mutation is, and P4d surviving on experience variation alone is a known weakness of that row, disclosed here rather than left to be discovered. WHY THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF M3: M3 breaks the SHAPE of the cap (a multiplier and a ceiling return), M6 leaves the shape exactly as D101 ruled it and breaks only which row of the table is read. A gate that checked the source text for 'Math.min(12' would catch M3 and never see M6. EXPECTED COLLATERAL: the pinned cfg is 18-35, so Q2..Q8 all stay GREEN. P1, P2, P3 GREEN. B1 GREEN.

name: M7 -> E4 is reverted: the dampened pace-clock note goes back to the V201 wording. It states D101's rate as a CAP rather than a rate, re-asserts '(physiological safety limit)' about a number that is this file's own coaching table and nothing more, and puts a mid-sentence em-dash in front of the athlete. Every prescribed second is untouched: this mutant ships a correct program described wrongly
anchor: note = `INT — Interval: Pace moves ${pp._weeklyGain} seconds per mile each week. That is the safe rate for your experience and age. Your full goal of ${goalFmt}/mi needs more weeks than this block has. The target for this block is ${reachFmt}/mi. Hit the prescribed pace precisely.`;
replacement: note = `INT — Interval: Pace capped at +${pp._weeklyGain}s/mi/week (physiological safety limit). Full goal of ${goalFmt}/mi requires more time — realistic target for this block is ${reachFmt}/mi. Hit the prescribed pace precisely.`;
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_pace_copy C1, which compares the note to coach's ruled E4 sentence TYPED IN THE GATE, with its numbers re-derived by hand from the entered 8:15 mile and the entered 10:30/1.5 mi goal. It must print a first miss beginning 'W1 reads |INT — Interval: Pace capped at'. C2 and C3 must go red alongside it and they are the reason C1 is not alone: C2 names the unsourced physiological claim, C3 names the copy-rule violation, and each of the three is a separate thing the ruling asked for, so a partial revert can only extinguish some of them. C1a must STAY GREEN — the dampened branch still fires 5 times on the pinned cfg; a red C1a would mean the sweep stopped exercising the branch and C1/C2/C3 would be vacuously red for the wrong reason. EXPECTED COLLATERAL: none in C4..C9 (different function) and none in g202_pace_anchor.js at all, because no prescribed second moves. B2 stays GREEN, and that is the sharpest thing about this mutant: HALF_MANNY's digest cannot see it.

name: M8 -> E5's goal scoping is reverted: the anchor card tells a pace-goal athlete that EVERY pace in the program comes from the anchor row. C4 must go red with it (the pinned card no longer matches coach's verbatim sentence). C5 must STAY GREEN and that is what separates the two halves of E5: chart goals were never wrong and are not being changed. C8 must also go red, because the clipboard still carries the scope the card just dropped; that is the mirror doing its job and is listed as EXPECTED COLLATERAL rather than as the target, since a reviewer who saw only C8 might reasonably re-edit runAnchorLine instead of runAnchorSentence. C6 stays GREEN: the dash is still gone. C9 stays GREEN. B2 GREEN.

name: M9 -> E6 is reverted: the rendered card keeps the ruled week-1 scope but the CLIPBOARD line drops it, so the text Mario copies out of the app makes a broader claim than the card he copied it from. The app is right on screen and wrong on paper

C8 must go red with it, printing a 'card true line false' miss on the first run_pace_goal form. WHY BOTH ROWS EXIST: C9 is a literal pin on one line, C8 is the equivalence between card and clipboard across all 30 forms; C9 alone could be satisfied by a hard-coded string and C8 alone is satisfied by making BOTH wrong, which is exactly what M8 does in the other direction. C4, C5, C6, C7 must all STAY GREEN — the rendered card is untouched — and a suite that only rendered the card would ship this mutant. C1..C3 GREEN. B2 GREEN. No prescribed value moves.

note: NAMED TRIP: g202_pace_copy C6, the row that sweeps 30 goal x provenance forms for a space-flanked hyphen, en dash or em dash, counting the structural 'XXX — Label:' prefix separately so the exemption can never launder a real violation. It must go red on exactly 5 rows (the 'entered' form of one pace goal and four chart goals) and its first miss must name an entered row. C4 must go red with it: the pinned PRT TING card is an entered form and no longer matches coach's verbatim sentence. C5 red too (HALF_MANNY is entered). C7 must STAY GREEN, and that is the point of the mutation: the SCOPE logic is untouched, so a gate that only checked which tail was appended would pass a card with a dash in it. WHY THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF M8: M8 breaks what the sentence CLAIMS, M10 breaks how it READS, and only one of the two is visible to a claim-checking oracle. C8, C9 GREEN. C1..C3 GREEN. B2 GREEN.

name: M11 -> the beginner exclusion is dropped from the clipboard mirror only. A beginner's card ends on its own sentence and takes neither tail (the beginner never trains off the entered mile at all), but the copied line now appends the week-1 scope anyway, so card and clipboard disagree for exactly one athlete class

This mutation is the defect this slice actually shipped on its first pass and then fixed, which is why it is in the file: the first cut of E6 keyed the clipboard scope on goalId only, the gate caught it, and the BUILD was changed rather than the gate. name: M12 -> the running maximum is dropped from the row reader. Every column is read as tabulated, so the one chart row that inverts (mile 12:00: half 845, marathon 825) now promises a marathon pace FASTER than the same athlete's half pace. Fourteen of fifteen rows are unaffected and the pinned athlete is unaffected, so the app is correct everywhere a reviewer is likely to look

replacement: var v = ROW_PACE_COLS.map(function(c){ run = +row[c.k]; return {d:c.d, p:run}; });

name: M13 -> the interpolation between chart columns goes linear instead of log. The shape is unchanged, the clamps and the running maximum survive, and the number moves by about 7 s/mi at 1.5 miles — enough to move every prescribed second in the block and small enough to read as rounding
note: NAMED TRIP: g202 Q2b, the row that RE-DERIVES the pinned anchor as 495 + (535-495) x ln(1.5)/ln(3.107) in the gate's own arithmetic. Q2 must go red with it (the literal measure printed from the surgery copy) and so must P1, which computes the log fraction for all 360 builds. WHY BOTH: Q2 is a literal pin and Q2b is the derivation, and a linear model that happened to agree at one distance would still fail the sweep. EXPECTED COLLATERAL: Q5, Q7, Q8 red (the after-grid hangs off the anchor), and g202_pace_copy C1 red, because the ruled note prints the block target and the gate derives 7:44/mi from the log model. R2 red as well: the beginner's DEFAULT row converts at 1.5 mi through the very log model this mutation replaces (690/735 reads 706.09 under log, 700.6786900806834 under linear), so that red is the gate working. R1 must STAY GREEN — rowPaceAt(row, 1.0) returns the mile column under either model, which is exactly why R1 alone can never see this. R3, R4 GREEN. B1 GREEN.

name: M14 -> D111 (E8) is reverted to the proportion it replaced: the interval pace goes back to weekPace x 0.95. Nothing looks missing — every card still prints a target a little faster than the goal — but the gap is no longer guide A's 4 seconds per 400m, and it drifts with the athlete's speed: about 3.75 s per 400 at a 5:00 mile and about 9 s per 400 at a 12:00 mile, more than twice what A prescribes for exactly the population this guide serves
anchor: const intPace    = weekPace ? Math.max(pp._realisticTarget - INT_PACE_GAIN_SEC_PER_MILE, weekPace - INT_PACE_GAIN_SEC_PER_MILE) : null;
replacement: const intPace    = weekPace ? Math.max(pp._realisticTarget * 0.95, weekPace * 0.95) : null;
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_int_doctrine D1, which measures the gap between the two numbers the card itself prints (the prescribed interval pace and the goal pace beside it) and requires it to be exactly 16 s/mi across goals from about 6:00 to 12:39/mi. A proportion cannot hold a constant gap across that span; D1b proves the two rules disagree at 5 of 6 hand goal paces, so D1 cannot be satisfied by both. D7 goes red with it (the pinned after-grid reads 484 again, not 493) and g202_pace_anchor Q8 goes red on the same two cards. D2 stays GREEN and MUST: it is pure hand arithmetic in A's units and the app is not in it — a suite that only checked D2 would ship this mutant. D4 follows the target, so the recovery band moves with it and stays self-consistent: the recovery rows do NOT catch this.

name: M15 -> the 16 s/mi is replaced by 4, the per-400m number used as if it were per mile. This is the transcription slip D111 is one conversion away from: guide A states the rule in seconds per 400m and the engine prescribes in seconds per mile
anchor: const INT_PACE_GAIN_SEC_PER_MILE = 16;   // 4 s per 400m x 4 quarters
replacement: const INT_PACE_GAIN_SEC_PER_MILE = 4;   // 4 s per 400m x 4 quarters
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_int_doctrine D1 — the printed gap becomes 4 s/mi instead of 16. The gate's own 16 is built from two typed factors (4 seconds per 400m, 4 quarters per mile) and never read from the app, so moving the app's constant moves one side only. D7 red. D2 stays GREEN for the same reason as M14. Recovery (D4) stays self-consistent and does not catch it.

name: M16 -> the cutback hold is dropped from the INT pace index: a cutback week reads its OWN week in the progression instead of the PRIOR one, so the card still prints "Cutback week. Same target as last week, fewer reps." while prescribing a target five seconds per mile faster than the week it claims to be repeating. The reduced rep count hides it: the session looks easier while the pace clock quietly tightened on the one week that is supposed to absorb the block. (This mutation replaces slice 3's E9 mutation, which after the slice 6 revert had no code left to mutate.)
anchor: const weekPace   = pp ? pp[(_cb && _ppIdx > 0) ? _ppIdx - 1 : _ppIdx] : null;  // D2b: effective index
replacement: const weekPace   = pp ? pp[_ppIdx] : null;  // D2b: effective index
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_int_doctrine D3, the cutback limb: 48 cutback cards across the lattice log a target their own sentence says is unchanged from the week before. D1 stays GREEN (the printed gap is still 16 s/mi on non-cutback cards, and a cutback card prints no goal pace), which is why D3 and not D1 is the declared target. D7 goes red with it on W4 (483 -> 478) and g202_pace_anchor Q8 stays GREEN: the two pinned cards are W1 and W6, neither a cutback week, so a suite pinned only on those two would ship this mutant. Labelled M16 after the V202 slice 7 renumber; before that renumber this file reused M8..M13 twice and no mutation could be selected by name.

name: M17 -> the recovery band collapses to the ratio the fixed 200m literal actually delivered. Measure found the old 'walk or jog 200m' was 0.685x the work interval across 11,880 of 11,880 INT sessions; this mutation keeps the new m:ss sentence and the new dose field and simply prescribes that measured ratio, so the card still LOOKS like it obeys guide A
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_int_doctrine D4, which recomputes the band by hand from the session's own target and the typed 2 and 2.5 multipliers, and D4b, which requires every printed band to sit inside A's 2 to 2.5 x the work interval (A 248-249, A 268-270, and both hand-transcribed table headers at doctrine/ptg2020_tables_p13_14_16_17.txt lines 9 and 41). D7 red on the pinned 4:05 to 5:06. D5 stays GREEN: the 200m literal really is gone, the sentence really does print m:ss to m:ss, and only the arithmetic lies. A gate that only asked whether the old string had been removed would ship this mutant.

name: M18 -> the rec band is dropped from the dose while the sentence keeps printing it. The athlete still reads the right recovery in the card, but every downstream reader of the structured dose (the log form, anything that later wants to compare prescribed against actual) sees an INT session with no recovery prescription at all
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_int_doctrine D4 ('dose carries no rec band') and D7 (the pinned band on all six weeks). D5/D5b stay GREEN because the printed sentence is untouched, which is exactly the asymmetry this mutation exists to expose: the ruling put the band on the ITEM as well as in the prose, and a gate reading only the prose cannot tell.

name: M19 -> E11 is reverted: the warm-up goes back to the '5 min easy warmup + cooldown' fragment that appears in neither guide. Guide A is silent on warm-up, so under D112 limb 2 guide B p8 governs, and B asks for 10-15 minutes or more plus 4-5 bursts of 15 to 30 seconds. Five minutes is a third of the floor before a Zone 5 session

note: NAMED TRIP: g202_int_doctrine D5b, which requires B p8's sentence verbatim on every INT card and the old fragment on none. The expected sentence is typed in the gate from coach's ruling, never read from the app. A0d cross-checks that B p8 still carries the source when the gitignored doctrine text is present. D4 and D7 stay GREEN: the recovery arithmetic is untouched, so only the warm-up row sees this.

name: M20 -> E7 is reverted: the clamp is dropped and the progression works on the ENTERED goal again, so an athlete whose goal is at or slower than the pace they already run at the goal distance is parked on the goal for the whole block. _originalTarget and _goalMet are untouched and still read correctly, so the metas look right and only the prescribed seconds are wrong
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_pace_anchor P5b, the row that says the class holds ONE pace and that pace is the gate's own HAND anchor. It must go red across the whole class (114 of 360 builds in this lattice) with a first miss of the form 'got [420 420 420 420 420 420], want 370.7 every week'. P5b is the declared target and not P5: P5 scopes itself to the IMPROVING segment and is untouched by this mutation, which is exactly why E7 needed its own row. EXPECTED COLLATERAL, DISCLOSED: none. P5d stays GREEN, and that is the point of listing it separately — _dampened is false on both sides of this mutation (rawImprovement is negative, weeklyImprovement is the same negative number, and the strict less-than is false either way), so a gate that only asserted the dampener would ship this mutant with an athlete prescribed slower work than they already run. P5e GREEN (_originalTarget reads enteredTarget directly). P5f and P5g GREEN: _goalMet is computed above the clamp and still true, so the note is still correct while the numbers under it are not. P1..P4 GREEN, Q1..Q8 GREEN (the pinned PRT TING cfg's goal is FASTER than its anchor, so E7 never reaches it). B1 GREEN: HALF_MANNY is NRC.

name: M21 -> E12 is reverted: the goal-already-met branch is removed, so the class falls through to the generic Zone 5 interval note. Every prescribed second is untouched. The athlete is told to build from 4 reps to 8 and given no word about the goal they entered being one they already beat

} else if(pp._goalMet) {
            note = 'Your goal pace is already within your current pace. This block holds your pace and builds your reps.';
note: NAMED TRIP: g202_pace_anchor P5f, which compares every non-cutback interval note in the class against coach's E12 sentence TYPED IN THE GATE. P5g must go red with it and is listed as the second half of the same claim rather than as collateral: P5g asserts the RENDERED string is byte-identical to the ruling and carries no mid-sentence dash, and the generic note this mutation restores contains ' — ' twice, so a revert that merely reworded E12 would be caught by P5f while a revert that dropped it entirely is caught by both. note: NAMED TRIP: g202_pace_copy C10, the appendix sweep. The goal-met x non-zero-shift class (57 of 293 INT cards on the 54-cfg lattice) loses the sentence. name: M24 -> ONE of the four copies of the ruled generic INT note takes the cap of 10 back. The other three still read 8, so the string looks maintained wherever a reviewer greps; the copy that regresses is the one on the progression path, which is the note the athlete with a pace goal actually reads.
